body.target_estimand: At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\), each labelled point in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) has a cohort-common treated conditional mean, and the causal target is \(\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\mathbb E[B_{si}(1)-B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]\), whose value is independent of the replica \(i\). For a joint panel law \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), this conditional interpretation and the common-replica equality are asserted only for \(P\)-almost every query \(z_0\).
body.estimand_functional: At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\), consistency, cohort-common treated-mean replication, and event-date transport identify \(\tau(z_0)=\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}\) for every labelled point \(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\). For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the deterministic experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) treats \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) as known specifications, while every outer MSE or interval rule is one \(\mathcal O\)-measurable rule selected before the unknown donor mean and labelled point. The marginal squared-risk scale is \(R_\star=R_{\mathrm{or}}\vee N^{-\lambda}\), with the iid spacing replacement on \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\). Donor upper bounds use only unbiasedness and covariance ellipticity; no donor fourth-moment or covariance-consistency condition is imposed. For a joint panel law, only the labelled tuple \(\xi_P(z_0)=(\mathbb K_{P,z_0};\mu_P(z_0),m,\Sigma_P(z_0))\) is placed in the fixed-query class, and only for marginal-almost-every query. No panel-induced conditional converse, null-query assertion, lower local modulus, or result for \(\lambda>1\) is claimed.

sampling_model.design: At each fixed admissible query, every exact design coordinate has conditional density between \(c_X\) and \(C_X\), and each cohort's design sequence is geometrically beta mixing. Fixed constants \(\eta_K\in(0,\delta_0]\) and \(k_K>0\) satisfy \(K(v)\ge k_K\) on \(\|v\|_2\le\eta_K\), while \(0<c_G<k_Kc_Xv_d\eta_K^d/4\). The iid subclass requires independence only of design dates.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort has \(n_s\) complete replicated unit histories. Conditional on the exact design, histories are independent across \((s,i)\), training responses have means \(m_s(X_{st})\), and treated outcomes have the common cohort mean \(\mu_s(z_0)\). Dependence among all coordinates within one history remains unrestricted.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency identifies observed event wealth with treated potential wealth. Event-date transport separately equates the untreated event mean with \(m_s(z_{0s})\); neither centering nor density overlap proves that causal restriction.
sampling_model.overlap: Queries are at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary. Strict slack \(\delta_0<1/2\) is used only by converse witnesses that displace an interior query.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Historical training coordinates are exact. Donor folds estimate only the external query center. Their mean-square control uses donor unbiasedness and the full elliptic covariance, with no fourth-moment assumption, covariance-consistency rate, deconvolution, response-calendar mixing, or calendar-score studentization.

Classical smooth-regression rates provide a benchmark but not the fixed-site replicated-response geometry or external generated query.
Strong convexity makes estimated-minimizer minimum-value perturbations second order, unlike the rough-Holder external-query modulus.
Generated covariates enter its training rows, whereas the present historical coordinates are exact and only the event query is generated.
Repeated-measurement deconvolution contaminates latent training coordinates; the center-only design here has no deconvolution phase.
Ordinary random-design smoothing does not separate replicated-site spacing from an external donor-location channel.
Pointwise local-polynomial theory motivates smoothing but not the bounded product-experiment nearest-site frontier.
Optimal local-polynomial kernels concern ordinary pointwise asymptotic efficiency, not this rough-Holder generated-query frontier.
Random-design sup-norm sharp estimation concerns global loss rather than conditional recovery at an external generated query.
Errors-in-variables regression contaminates all training covariates and therefore has a deconvolution rate absent here.
Smooth generated-regressor expansions do not cover the nonsmooth rough-Holder query modulus or minimax converse.
The coverage-to-testing benchmark underlies the honest-length converse but has no external donor-location channel.
Ordered-modulus intervals in known regression experiments do not cover generated-center uncertainty.
Bias-aware ordinary-regression intervals contain no external full-covariance donor query.
Dependent-data resampling is not invoked because the interval concentrates complete unit histories and uses design mixing only for occupancy.
Many-control panel asymptotics motivate cross-unit replication but do not give the generated-query optimal-recovery frontier.
Dependent synthetic-control prediction intervals do not supply complete-unit concentration plus a donor-location expected-length converse.
Conformal synthetic-control inference uses a different exchangeability and prediction architecture, not generated-query expected-length minimaxity.
Synthetic-control practice motivates transparent causal assumptions but does not validate event-date transport.
Panel causal-model surveys locate identifying assumptions but do not derive this generated-query statistical frontier.

body.tldr: For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the paper proves a three-channel Stat frontier for realized-path causal buy-and-hold wealth: event-outcome replication, query-conditional calendar spacing, and full-covariance donor location. Historical proxy paths are exact and only the external event query is generated. The Gram threshold is fixed below the explicit local kernel-ball mass, and donor upper bounds require only unbiasedness and covariance ellipticity. A deterministic fixed-design rule may use known \(X,z_0,\Sigma\); every outer estimator and interval is one observable rule selected before the unknown donor mean. Panel conclusions transfer only through the labelled tuple \(\xi_P(z_0)\) at marginal-almost-every query.

project_justification.gap: Classical smooth regression and Gaussian optimal recovery do not combine finitely many exact design sites carrying replicated responses with an external full-covariance generated query. Generated-covariate and deconvolution models instead alter training coordinates, and ordinary interval theory has no donor-location expected-length converse.
project_justification.niche: The center-only experiment separates three sources of difficulty. Conditional density and design mixing control occupancy of an explicit kernel ball; complete-unit concentration handles arbitrary within-history response dependence; and covariance control of donor means yields a rough-Holder \(N^{-\lambda}\) risk channel without any donor tail assumption.
project_justification.fill: The note supplies a known-specification fixed-design recovery result, a feasible unknown-query marginal estimator, and a total honest interval for \(0<\lambda\le1\). Explicit treated, clustered-spacing, iid-spacing, and finite-support donor witnesses match the rates. The causal bridge is the labelled point \(\xi_P(z_0)\), constructed only on a marginally conull query set.

body.related_work:
\textbf{Conditional frontier comparison.} Donoho's known Gaussian convex optimal-recovery experiment \cite{Donoho1994} and Stone's smooth-regression benchmark \cite{Stone1982} do not supply the bounded multiple-response fixed-design and full-covariance donor-location product experiment here. Exact training coordinates make a root-\(N\) query displacement change a merely \(\lambda\)-Holder evaluation by \(N^{-\lambda/2}\), unlike the second-order minimum-value perturbation under strong convexity in Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov \cite{AkhavanGogolashviliTsybakov2024}. The panel bridge is deliberately one-sided and marginal-almost-everywhere.

\textbf{Marginal phase comparison.} Stone's ordinary random-design rate uses growing distinct sites \cite{Stone1982}; here responses are replicated at only \(T\) exact sites, producing iid spacing \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\) and geometric-mixing spacing \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\). The smoothing term is dominated for fixed \(S\). Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle generate training-row covariates \cite{MammenRotheSchienle2012}, and Delaigle, Hall, and Meister study noisy training coordinates and deconvolution \cite{DelaigleHallMeister2008}; neither has the center-only donor channel \(N^{-\lambda}\).

\textbf{Honest-length comparison.} Low gives the coverage-to-testing benchmark \cite{Low1997}; Armstrong and Kolesar develop ordered-modulus and bias-aware ordinary-regression intervals \cite{ArmstrongKolesar2018,ArmstrongKolesar2020}; and Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik study dependent synthetic-control prediction intervals \cite{CattaneoFengTitiunik2021}. The present interval concentrates one bounded complete history per unit, adds an explicit rough-Holder donor radius, and is total on geometry failures. It uses neither response-calendar mixing nor estimated-variance division, and donor-only perturbations create the additional \(N^{-\lambda/2}\) honest-length lower channel.
body.interpretation: The causal target and statistical functional remain distinct. The labelled fixed-query law identifies \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\); consistency and event-date transport then prove equality with \(\tau(z_0)\). Donor uncertainty dominates when \(N^{-\lambda}\) exceeds treated replication and conditional spacing. Known \(X,z_0,\Sigma\) are available only in the deterministic experiment; revealing \(z_0\) to the outer rule would erase the donor channel. The finite-support moment calculations belong to lower-bound witnesses and are not restrictions on the model.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Every constructive headline is restricted to \(0<\lambda\le1\), fixed dimension, finitely many cohorts, and fixed admissible queries; panel-law transfer through \(\xi_P(z_0)\) is only marginal-almost-everywhere. Design-conditional centering rules out the former common-design-shock witness, so that audit is not retained as a numbered result. The active primitives nevertheless do not fix conditional treated-outcome variance or a limiting calendar long-run variance. Therefore exact constants at phase intersections remain open. Higher-order smoothness, growing dimension, adaptation, and uniform-in-query bands require separate arguments.
body.honest_scope: Event-date transport is untestable. The centering restriction imposes common treated means and design-invariant conditional means, but not identical replica distributions, within-history independence, or response-calendar mixing. The interval uses whole-unit bounded-range concentration, a rough-Holder donor radius based on mean-square covariance control, and the full-range fallback. The donor fourth moment is not assumed. Fixed-design decisions know \(X,z_0,\Sigma\); outer decisions do not know \(z_0\). Causal coverage and expected-length upper conclusions transfer only through the labelled tuple \(\xi_P(z_0)\) on a marginally conull query set.
